statement: >= 90% of training compute of the 10 largest known 2027 training runs belongs to organisations headquartered in the two leading jurisdictions (Epoch AI; snapshot 2028-03-31)
status_at_phase_end: As of end-2025 all known training runs above 1e26 FLOP (Grok 3 ~3.5e26, GPT-4.5 ~3.8e26, Grok 4 ~5e26) belonged to Bloc A organisations; ~30+ models above 1e25 FLOP from ~12 developers, essentially all in Bloc A or Bloc B. GPU-cluster compute ~75% Bloc A / ~15% Bloc B (May 2025). The two-bloc concentration the indicator measures was near-total; the main uncertainty is undisclosed compute for frontier runs.

items.summary: Epoch AI: over 25 publicly announced models from 11 developers exceed 1e25 FLOP (GPT-4 scale), with roughly two new such models per month in 2024; the developers are concentrated in the two leading jurisdictions.
items.detail: Epoch Data Insight 'Over 20/30 AI models have been trained at the scale of GPT-4' (Rahman, Heindrich, Owen, Emberson), first published 2025-01-30. Developers reviewed include Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, xAI, NVIDIA, ByteDance, plus Bloc B labs via CompassRank.

items.summary: A Bloc A developer released the first publicly known model estimated above 1e26 FLOP (~3.5e26), a new training-compute record.
items.detail: xAI Grok 3, released 2025-02-17, trained on the Colossus cluster (Memphis); Epoch estimate ~3.5e26 FLOP (per Epoch-derived tables; model page not directly verified).

items.summary: Another Bloc A developer released a model estimated at ~3.8e26 FLOP, the second known run above 1e26.
items.detail: OpenAI GPT-4.5, released 2025-02-27; Epoch estimate ~3.8e26 FLOP (Epoch-derived tables).

items.summary: Research forecast: ~2 public models above 1e26 FLOP as of April 2025, rising to a median 81 (90% CI 45-148) by end-2028; models within one order of magnitude of the largest run stay at ~14-16 per year - i.e. the top tier remains a small club.
items.detail: Kumar et al., 'Trends in Frontier AI Model Count: A Forecast to 2028', arXiv 2504.16138 (April 2025; day approximate).

items.summary: Epoch AI: as of May 2025, Bloc A hosts about three-quarters of global GPU-cluster performance and Bloc B about 15%; traditional HPC leaders elsewhere play marginal roles. ~90% of AI-cluster compute sits in the two leading jurisdictions.
items.detail: Epoch Data Insight 'The Bloc A hosts the majority of GPU cluster performance, followed by Bloc B' (Pilz, Rahman, Sanders, Emberson, Heim), 2025-06-05; based on the 'Trends in AI supercomputers' dataset (April 2025). Verified.

items.summary: Epoch update: over 30 models from 12 developers above 1e25 FLOP as of June 2025. Large-scale (>1e23) models: over half from Bloc A, about a quarter from Bloc B (share growing).
items.detail: Epoch 'models-over-1e25-flop' insight updated 2025-06-06; Large-Scale AI Models dataset page (updated July 2025). Bloc C 46, Bloc G 31 large-scale models cumulative.

items.summary: A Bloc A developer released the largest known training run of 2025 (~5e26 FLOP; ~$490M compute cost, ~310 GWh), which remained the record through year-end.
items.detail: xAI Grok 4, released 2025-07-09. Epoch Data Insight 'What did it take to train Grok 4?' (2025-09-12, verified) and Epoch model page (5.0e26 FLOP).

items.summary: Several Bloc A frontier developers did not disclose training compute for their 2025 flagship models, and Bloc B compute estimates are sparse; the top-10 list is therefore partly estimated from cluster size and benchmark imputation.
items.detail: Epoch documentation: compute for many frontier models imputed from benchmarks or hardware ('Likely' ~10x, 'Speculative' ~30x uncertainty).
